author: reek
body: Reservoir sampling promises one thing: after streaming n items through a reservoir of capacity k, every item that went past has the same probability of being in the sample. Not a similar probability. The same one. That is the whole reason to use Algorithm R rather than keeping the first k.

author: reek
body: The measurement is the promise. Stream the same twenty items through a five-slot reservoir under many different seeds and count how often each item survives. Uniform sampling puts every item in the sample about a quarter of the time. A structured one favours some positions and starves others, and the spread between the luckiest and the unluckiest item is what shows it.

author: reek
body: Each trial builds a fresh reservoir: reservoir-add writes surviving slots with list-set-at, which mutates in place, so a reused one would carry the previous trial's contents.
